name: Sprint intervals
steps: Find a flat 50-meter stretch of ground.
Sprint at maximum effort for 30 seconds.
Walk back slowly to recover for 60 seconds.
Repeat for 6–10 rounds.
Cool down with 5 minutes of light jogging.
mistakes: Skipping the warm-up and pulling a muscle.
Sprinting on uneven or slippery surfaces.
Not allowing enough recovery between sprints.

name: Running (6 mph / 10 min-mile)
steps: Start with a 5-minute brisk walk to warm up.
Settle into a pace where breathing is heavy but controlled.
Land on your midfoot with a slight forward lean.
Swing your arms naturally and keep shoulders relaxed.
Cool down with 5 minutes of walking.
mistakes: Starting too fast and burning out early.
Over-striding and landing on your heel.
Tensing your shoulders and wasting energy.

name: Jogging (12 min-mile)
steps: Start with 3 minutes of walking.
Begin jogging at a conversational pace.
Keep your steps short and light.
Breathe rhythmically through your nose and mouth.
Aim for 20–30 minutes without stopping.
mistakes: Running too fast for a jog and getting tired quickly.
Looking down at the ground instead of ahead.
Clenching your fists tightly.

name: Stair sprints (stadium/building)
steps: Find a staircase with at least 3 flights.
Run up the stairs as fast as you can safely.
Walk back down to recover.
Use the handrail for safety if needed.
Repeat for 8–12 rounds.
mistakes: Skipping steps to go faster and risking a fall.
Leaning too far forward and losing balance.
Not walking down carefully during recovery.

name: Cycling (fast, 19–22 km/h)
steps: Adjust your seat so your leg is almost straight at the bottom of the pedal stroke.
Warm up with 5 minutes of easy pedaling.
Increase speed to 19–22 km/h and hold it.
Keep your core engaged and back neutral.
Shift gears to maintain consistent effort on hills.
mistakes: Having the seat too low and straining your knees.
Gripping the handlebars too tightly.
Ignoring traffic and surroundings when outdoors.

name: Cycling (moderate, 16–19 km/h)
steps: Set your seat height so your leg is almost fully extended at the bottom.
Start pedaling at a comfortable pace.
Maintain a speed of 16–19 km/h on flat ground.
Keep your back straight and elbows slightly bent.
Breathe steadily and enjoy the ride.
mistakes: Pedaling in too high a gear and tiring your knees.
Slouching forward and straining your lower back.
Not wearing a helmet for safety.

name: Hill hiking
steps: Choose a trail with a steady incline.
Walk at a pace that elevates your heart rate.
Take shorter steps on steep sections.
Use trekking poles for extra stability if available.
Stay hydrated and take breaks as needed.
mistakes: Wearing flat or slippery shoes.
Going too fast downhill and hurting your knees.
Not bringing enough water.

name: Brisk walking (15 min-mile)
steps: Stand tall with your shoulders back and chin level.
Walk at a pace where your breathing is slightly elevated.
Swing your arms naturally at your sides.
Aim for about 100 steps per minute.
Walk for at least 30 minutes for best results.
mistakes: Walking too slowly to get any cardiovascular benefit.
Looking down at the ground constantly.
Taking steps that are too long and straining your hips.

name: Incline walking
steps: Find a hill or set a treadmill to 8–12% incline.
Walk at a moderate pace keeping your posture upright.
Push through your heels to engage your glutes.
Keep your arms swinging naturally.
Walk for 20–30 minutes.
mistakes: Holding onto the treadmill rails and leaning back.
Bending forward at the waist.
Starting with too steep an incline.

name: Burpees
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Drop into a squat and place your hands on the floor.
Jump your feet back into a plank position.
Do one push-up, then jump your feet back to your hands.
Leap straight up with arms overhead.
mistakes: Skipping the push-up to rush through reps.
Landing with locked knees on the jump.
Letting your hips sag during the plank.

name: Mountain climbers
steps: Start in a high plank with hands under shoulders.
Drive one knee toward your chest quickly.
Switch legs in a running motion.
Keep your hips level and core tight.
Maintain a fast but controlled pace.
mistakes: Bouncing your hips up and down.
Placing your hands too far forward.
Holding your breath instead of breathing steadily.

name: High knees (in place)
steps: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Drive one knee up to hip height while pumping your opposite arm.
Quickly switch legs in a running motion.
Stay on the balls of your feet.
Keep your core engaged throughout.
mistakes: Leaning too far backward.
Not lifting your knees high enough.
Landing flat-footed instead of on your toes.

name: Jumping jacks (vigorous)
steps: Stand with feet together and arms at your sides.
Jump your feet apart while raising your arms overhead.
Jump feet back together and lower your arms.
Maintain a steady, fast rhythm.
Keep your core engaged and land softly.
mistakes: Not fully extending your arms overhead.
Landing with flat feet instead of on the balls of your feet.
Going too slowly to get the heart rate up.

name: Squat jumps
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Lower into a squat until thighs are parallel to the floor.
Explode upward, jumping as high as you can.
Land softly back into the squat position.
Repeat immediately without pausing.
mistakes: Landing with stiff legs and jarring your knees.
Not squatting deep enough before jumping.
Letting your knees cave inward on the landing.

name: Skater hops
steps: Stand on your right foot with a slight bend in your knee.
Hop sideways to the left landing on your left foot.
Swing your right leg behind your left ankle.
Immediately hop back to the right.
Keep your chest up and arms swinging for balance.
mistakes: Hopping too far and losing balance.
Landing with a straight leg instead of a soft bend.
Not engaging your core for stability.

name: Shadow boxing
steps: Stand in a boxing stance with your dominant foot slightly back.
Throw jabs, crosses, hooks, and uppercuts into the air.
Stay light on your feet and move around.
Keep your guard up near your chin between punches.
Alternate 3-minute rounds with 1-minute rest.
mistakes: Dropping your hands between punches.
Standing flat-footed instead of staying mobile.
Throwing punches with only your arms instead of using your whole body.

name: Home stair climbing
steps: Find a staircase in your home with at least one flight.
Walk or jog up the stairs at a steady pace.
Walk back down carefully to recover.
Repeat for 10–15 minutes.
Use the handrail if you need extra balance.
mistakes: Rushing down the stairs and risking a fall.
Skipping steps on the way up before you are ready.
Wearing socks or slippery footwear.

name: Bear crawl
steps: Start on all fours with knees hovering just above the ground.
Move your right hand and left foot forward together.
Then move your left hand and right foot forward.
Keep your back flat and hips low.
Crawl forward for 10 meters, then turn and crawl back.
mistakes: Lifting your hips too high into a downward dog.
Moving the same-side hand and foot together.
Holding your breath during the movement.

name: Jump rope (fast, 120–160/min)
steps: Hold the rope handles at hip height with elbows close to your body.
Swing the rope using your wrists, not your shoulders.
Jump just high enough to clear the rope.
Land softly on the balls of your feet.
Aim for 120–160 jumps per minute.
mistakes: Jumping too high and wasting energy.
Swinging from the shoulders instead of the wrists.
Landing on your heels instead of the balls of your feet.

name: Jump rope (moderate)
steps: Hold the rope handles loosely at hip height.
Rotate the rope with small wrist circles.
Jump with both feet, clearing the rope by about 2 cm.
Land on the balls of your feet with soft knees.
Keep a steady rhythm for 3-minute intervals.
mistakes: Using your whole arm to swing the rope.
Jumping too high off the ground.
Tensing your shoulders instead of staying relaxed.

name: Push-up (vigorous sets)
steps: Start in a plank with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower your body until your chest is just above the floor.
Keep your elbows at about 45 degrees from your body.
Push back up to the starting position explosively.
Do sets of 10–15 reps with 30 seconds rest between sets.
mistakes: Letting your hips sag toward the floor.
Flaring your elbows straight out to the sides.
Not going low enough to get full range of motion.

name: Pull-up
steps: Hang from a bar with palms facing away, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull your body up until your chin clears the bar.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top.
Lower yourself slowly to a full dead hang.
Repeat for as many reps as you can with good form.
mistakes: Using momentum to swing your body up.
Not going to full extension at the bottom.
Gripping too wide and straining your shoulders.

name: Chin-up
steps: Hang from a bar with palms facing toward you, hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull yourself up until your chin passes the bar.
Focus on squeezing your biceps at the top.
Lower yourself under control to a full dead hang.
Repeat for as many quality reps as possible.
mistakes: Kicking your legs to generate momentum.
Using a partial range of motion.
Letting your shoulders shrug up toward your ears.

name: Dips (parallel/chair)
steps: Place your hands on parallel bars or the edge of a sturdy chair.
Lower your body by bending your elbows to about 90 degrees.
Keep your elbows pointing backward, not outward.
Press back up to full arm extension.
Use your legs for support if needed by keeping feet on the ground.
mistakes: Flaring your elbows outward and straining your shoulders.
Dropping too deep and overstretching the shoulder joint.
Locking your elbows aggressively at the top.

name: Pistol squat (progression)
steps: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended straight in front.
Slowly lower yourself by bending your standing knee.
Keep your heel flat on the ground and your chest up.
Go as low as you can, then push back up.
Hold onto a doorframe or chair for balance as you learn.
mistakes: Letting your knee collapse inward on the standing leg.
Rising up on your toes instead of keeping the heel down.
Rushing the movement instead of going slow and controlled.

name: Walking lunges
steps: Stand tall and step forward with one leg.
Lower your hips until both knees are at 90 degrees.
Push off your front foot and step forward with the other leg.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged.
Continue for 20 steps, rest, and repeat.
mistakes: Front knee going past the toes excessively.
Leaning your torso forward instead of staying upright.
Taking steps that are too short.

name: Plank
steps: Get into a forearm plank with elbows under your shoulders.
Keep your body in a perfectly straight line from head to heels.
Engage your core by pulling your belly button toward your spine.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
Start with 30-second holds and build up over time.
mistakes: Letting your hips sag toward the floor.
Piking your hips up too high.
Holding your breath instead of breathing normally.

name: Crunches
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your fingertips lightly behind your ears.
Curl your shoulders off the floor using your abs.
Hold the top position for one second.
Lower back down with control.
mistakes: Pulling on your neck with your hands.
Using momentum to swing up instead of engaging your abs.
Coming up too high and turning it into a sit-up.

name: Leg raises
steps: Lie flat on your back with legs straight.
Place your hands under your lower back for support.
Slowly raise both legs until they point straight up.
Lower them back down without touching the floor.
Keep your lower back pressed into the ground throughout.
mistakes: Arching your lower back off the ground.
Swinging your legs instead of moving them with control.
Bending your knees to make it easier.

name: Glute bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Push through your heels to lift your hips off the ground.
Squeeze your glutes hard at the top.
Hold for 2 seconds, then lower back down.
Repeat for 15–20 reps.
mistakes: Pushing through your toes instead of your heels.
Arching your lower back instead of using your glutes.
Not squeezing at the top of the movement.

name: Superman hold
steps: Lie face down with arms extended in front of you.
Lift your arms, chest, and legs off the ground simultaneously.
Squeeze your lower back muscles at the top.
Hold for 3–5 seconds, then lower down.
Repeat for 10–12 reps.
mistakes: Jerking your body up instead of lifting with control.
Holding your breath during the hold.
Lifting too high and straining your neck.

name: Treadmill running (6 mph+)
steps: Step onto the treadmill and set it to a walking speed to warm up.
Gradually increase speed to 6 mph or faster.
Maintain upright posture and a natural arm swing.
Keep your eyes forward, not down at your feet.
Cool down with 5 minutes of walking.
mistakes: Holding onto the handrails while running.
Starting at too high a speed without warming up.
Overstriding and landing heavily on your heels.

name: Stair climber machine
steps: Step onto the machine and grip the side rails lightly.
Set a moderate pace and begin stepping.
Keep your posture upright and avoid leaning on the handles.
Step with your full foot on each pedal.
Increase speed or resistance as your fitness improves.
mistakes: Leaning heavily on the handles and reducing the workout.
Taking tiny steps instead of full strides.
Setting the speed too high and losing proper form.

name: Rowing machine (vigorous)
steps: Sit on the rower and strap your feet in securely.
Push with your legs first, then lean back slightly and pull the handle to your chest.
Reverse the motion: extend your arms, lean forward, then bend your knees.
Maintain a powerful, fast rhythm.
Aim for high intensity intervals of 500 meters.
mistakes: Pulling with your arms before your legs fully extend.
Hunching your back during the pull.
Rushing the recovery phase.

name: Stationary bike (vigorous)
steps: Adjust the seat height so your leg is almost straight at the bottom.
Set the resistance to a challenging level.
Pedal at high speed for 30-second intervals.
Recover with slower pedaling for 60 seconds.
Repeat intervals for 20–30 minutes.
mistakes: Having the seat too low and straining your knees.
Bouncing in the saddle from too little resistance.
Gripping the handlebars too tightly.

name: Rowing machine (moderate)
steps: Sit on the rower and strap your feet in securely.
Push with your legs, lean back, and pull the handle to your lower chest.
Reverse the motion smoothly and under control.
Maintain a steady, sustainable pace.
Row for 20–30 minutes continuously.
mistakes: Rounding your back during the pull phase.
Using only your arms instead of driving with your legs.
Setting the damper too high and tiring quickly.

name: Stationary bike (moderate)
steps: Adjust the seat to proper height.
Set a moderate resistance level.
Pedal at a steady, comfortable pace.
Keep your core engaged and posture upright.
Ride for 30–45 minutes.
mistakes: Slouching forward over the handlebars.
Setting the resistance too low for any benefit.
Pedaling only with your toes instead of your whole foot.

name: Elliptical trainer
steps: Step onto the machine and grip the moving handles.
Push and pull the handles while pedaling smoothly.
Keep your posture upright and core engaged.
Adjust resistance for desired intensity.
Exercise for 30–40 minutes.
mistakes: Leaning heavily on the handles.
Setting resistance too low for any cardiovascular benefit.
Moving too slowly without enough intensity.

name: Treadmill incline walk
steps: Set the treadmill to 8–15% incline.
Walk at a speed of 5–6 km/h.
Keep your posture upright and avoid holding the rails.
Push through your heels to engage your glutes.
Walk for 20–30 minutes.
mistakes: Holding onto the handrails and leaning back.
Bending forward at the waist.
Setting the incline too high too soon.

name: Lat pulldown
steps: Sit at the machine with thighs secured under the pads.
Grip the bar wider than shoulder width with palms facing away.
Pull the bar down smoothly to your upper chest.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the bottom.
Release the bar slowly back to the starting position.
mistakes: Pulling the bar behind your neck.
Using body momentum to swing the weight down.
Gripping too narrow and limiting lat engagement.

name: Leg press
steps: Sit in the machine with your feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety handles carefully.
Lower the platform toward you by bending your knees.
Push the platform away by extending your legs.
Do not lock your knees fully at the top.
mistakes: Placing your feet too high or too low on the platform.
Letting your knees cave inward.
Locking your knees at the top of each rep.

name: Chest press machine
steps: Adjust the seat height so the handles are at chest level.
Grip the handles with a comfortable width.
Push the handles forward until your arms are almost fully extended.
Slowly return to the starting position.
Repeat for 10–12 reps per set.
mistakes: Arching your back off the pad.
Flaring your elbows too wide.
Not controlling the weight on the way back.

name: Seated cable row
steps: Sit at the cable row machine with feet on the foot pads.
Grab the handle with both hands and sit upright.
Pull the handle toward your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Extend your arms back slowly to the starting position.
Keep your torso still throughout the movement.
mistakes: Rounding your back during the pull.
Leaning too far back to use momentum.
Not squeezing the shoulder blades at the end of the pull.

name: Ab crunch machine
steps: Sit in the machine and adjust the pad to rest on your upper chest.
Place your feet flat on the floor or foot pads.
Crunch forward by contracting your abs.
Hold the bottom position for one second.
Return slowly to the starting position.
mistakes: Using too much weight and pulling with your arms.
Moving your hips instead of curling your upper body.
Rushing through reps without feeling the contraction.

name: Kettlebell swings
steps: Stand with feet wider than shoulder-width, kettlebell on the floor between your feet.
Hinge at your hips and grip the kettlebell with both hands.
Swing it back between your legs, then thrust your hips forward explosively.
Let the kettlebell float to chest height with straight arms.
Control the swing back down and repeat without pausing.
mistakes: Squatting instead of hinging at the hips.
Using your arms to lift the kettlebell instead of hip drive.
Rounding your lower back during the swing.

name: Clean & press
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell on the floor.
Grip the bar just outside your knees and clean it to your shoulders in one motion.
Dip your knees slightly and press the bar overhead.
Lock out your arms fully at the top.
Lower the bar back to your shoulders, then to the floor with control.
mistakes: Catching the bar with bent wrists.
Not fully extending the bar overhead.
Using too much weight before mastering the technique.

name: Dumbbell HIIT circuit
steps: Choose 4–5 dumbbell exercises like thrusters, rows, and lunges.
Perform each exercise for 40 seconds at high intensity.
Rest 20 seconds between exercises.
Complete 3–4 rounds of the full circuit.
Cool down with light stretching.
mistakes: Sacrificing form for speed.
Using dumbbells that are too heavy for fast circuits.
Not resting enough between rounds.

name: Barbell squat
steps: Position the bar across your upper traps and step back from the rack.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, toes slightly turned out.
Brace your core and sit down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Drive up through your heels to standing.
Re-rack the bar carefully after your set.
mistakes: Knees caving inward during the squat.
Not reaching parallel depth.
Excessive forward lean and rounding the back.

name: Deadlift
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell over your mid-foot.
Hinge at the hips and grip the bar just outside your knees.
Keep your back flat and drive through your heels to stand up.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and stand tall.
Lower the bar back to the floor by hinging at the hips.
mistakes: Rounding your lower back during the lift.
Pulling with your arms instead of driving with your legs.
Jerking the bar off the floor instead of lifting smoothly.

name: Dumbbell walking lunges
steps: Hold a dumbbell in each hand at your sides.
Step forward with one leg and lower into a lunge.
Push off your front foot to step forward with the other leg.
Keep your torso upright and core engaged.
Continue for 20 steps, rest, and repeat.
mistakes: Letting the dumbbells swing as you walk.
Leaning your torso forward instead of staying upright.
Taking steps that are too short.

name: Farmer's carry
steps: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand.
Stand tall with your shoulders back and core tight.
Walk forward with short, controlled steps.
Keep the weights from swinging by engaging your core.
Walk for 30–40 meters, rest, and repeat.
mistakes: Letting your shoulders round forward.
Taking steps that are too long and losing balance.
Using weights that are too light to be effective.

name: Bench press
steps: Lie flat on the bench with your feet firmly on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Unrack the bar and lower it to your mid-chest with control.
Press the bar back up to lockout.
Re-rack the bar carefully after your set.
mistakes: Bouncing the bar off your chest.
Arching your back excessively off the bench.
Not having a spotter when lifting heavy.

name: Overhead press
steps: Hold the bar at shoulder height with a grip just outside your shoulders.
Brace your core and press the bar straight overhead.
Lock out your arms fully at the top.
Lower the bar back to shoulder height with control.
Keep your head slightly back as the bar passes your face.
mistakes: Leaning too far back to cheat the weight up.
Pressing the bar forward instead of straight up.
Not bracing your core and using your lower back.

name: Barbell row
steps: Stand with feet hip-width apart, barbell in front of you.
Hinge at the hips until your torso is at about 45 degrees.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width.
Pull the bar to your lower chest, squeezing your shoulder blades.
Lower the bar under control back to arms length.
mistakes: Rounding your back during the row.
Using momentum to jerk the bar up.
Not pulling the bar high enough to fully contract the back.

name: Step-ups on box/chair
steps: Stand facing a sturdy box, bench, or chair.
Step up with one foot, pressing through your heel.
Bring your other foot up to stand on the box.
Step back down with control, one foot at a time.
Alternate leading legs each rep.
mistakes: Using a surface that is not stable and could tip.
Pushing off with the back foot instead of driving through the front heel.
Leaning forward instead of standing tall.

name: Resistance band circuit
steps: Choose 4–5 resistance band exercises like squats, rows, and presses.
Perform each exercise for 12–15 reps.
Rest 30 seconds between exercises.
Complete 2–3 rounds of the full circuit.
Focus on slow, controlled movements to maintain tension.
mistakes: Using a band that is too light to create resistance.
Letting the band snap back instead of controlling the return.
Rushing through reps without maintaining tension.

name: Wall sit
steps: Stand with your back flat against a wall.
Slide down until your thighs are parallel to the floor.
Keep your knees at a 90-degree angle directly over your ankles.
Hold the position and breathe steadily.
Start with 30-second holds and build up over time.
mistakes: Letting your knees go past your toes.
Placing your hands on your thighs for support.
Holding your breath instead of breathing normally.

name: Kegel Hold
steps: Sit or lie down comfortably with your knees slightly apart.
Find the pelvic floor muscles: the ones you would use to stop yourself passing wind or urine mid-flow.
Squeeze and lift those muscles inward and upward, without clenching your glutes, thighs or abs.
Hold for 5 to 10 seconds while breathing normally.
Release fully and rest for the same length of time before the next rep.
Do the sets listed in your program notes. Quality of the squeeze beats the count.
mistakes: Holding your breath or bearing down instead of lifting.
Squeezing your glutes, thighs or stomach to fake the movement.
Skipping the release phase — the muscle needs to fully relax between reps.
Practising while urinating, which can interfere with bladder emptying.

name: Standing hamstring stretch
steps: Stand tall and step one foot a short pace forward, heel down, toes up.
Keep that leg straight and hinge forward from the hips, not the waist.
Rest both hands on the front thigh and keep your back flat.
Breathe out and settle into the stretch until you feel a firm pull, never pain.
Hold 30 seconds, then swap legs. Two rounds each side.
mistakes: Rounding the back instead of hinging at the hips.
Bouncing to push deeper, which makes the muscle tighten.
Holding your breath while you stretch.

name: Standing quad stretch
steps: Stand next to a wall and rest one hand on it for balance.
Bend one knee and take that ankle in your hand behind you.
Draw the heel toward your glute and keep both knees close together.
Push the hip of the stretching leg gently forward and stand tall.
Hold 30 seconds, then swap sides. Two rounds each.
mistakes: Letting the knee drift out to the side.
Arching the lower back instead of tucking the hips.
Yanking the ankle rather than easing it in.

name: Kneeling hip flexor stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front, knee over ankle.
Put something soft under the down knee if the floor is hard.
Squeeze the glute of the kneeling leg and tuck your hips under.
Shift your weight slightly forward, keeping your chest upright.
Hold 30 seconds each side. Two rounds.
mistakes: Leaning the chest forward instead of tucking the hips.
Letting the front knee travel past the toes.
Skipping the glute squeeze, which is what makes this work.

name: Cat-cow spinal flow
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Breathe in and drop your belly, lifting your chest and tailbone.
Breathe out and round the spine, tucking your chin and tailbone.
Move slowly with the breath, one cycle every four to five seconds.
Do 10 slow cycles. Great as a warm-up or a desk-day reset.
mistakes: Rushing the movement instead of following the breath.
Locking the elbows and shrugging the shoulders.
Forcing range through the neck rather than the whole spine.

name: Child's pose
steps: Kneel with your big toes together and knees roughly hip-width apart.
Sit your hips back toward your heels.
Walk your hands forward and let your forehead rest down.
Let the ribs sink between the thighs and breathe into your back.
Hold 45 to 60 seconds. Use it to cool down after any session.
mistakes: Holding tension in the shoulders instead of letting them soften.
Forcing the hips down if the knees complain — widen them instead.
Shallow chest breathing rather than slow belly breaths.

name: Doorway chest stretch
steps: Stand in a doorway and place a forearm flat on the frame, elbow at shoulder height.
Step the same-side foot through the doorway.
Turn your chest gently away from that arm.
Keep the shoulder down, away from your ear.
Hold 30 seconds each side. Two rounds — ideal after a pressing session.
mistakes: Letting the shoulder ride up toward the ear.
Pushing until it pinches at the front of the shoulder.
Twisting the lower back instead of rotating the chest.

name: Neck and shoulder release
steps: Sit or stand tall and let your arms hang heavy.
Tip one ear toward that shoulder until you feel a gentle pull.
For more, reach the opposite hand down toward the floor.
Keep your jaw loose and breathe slowly.
Hold 20 to 30 seconds each side. Repeat twice — good for phone and desk neck.
mistakes: Pulling hard on the head with your hand.
Rolling the neck in full circles, which grinds the joints.
Hunching the opposite shoulder up as you tilt.

name: Full-body mobility flow
steps: Start standing. Roll the shoulders back five times.
Do 10 slow bodyweight squats to the depth you own comfortably.
Step into a lunge and rotate your chest over the front leg, five each side.
Move into cat-cow for five cycles.
Finish with 10 slow hip circles each direction.
Run through twice before training, or once on a rest day.
mistakes: Treating it as a workout and rushing for a burn.
Holding the breath through the harder positions.
Pushing into sharp pain instead of stopping at firm tension.
